thread: Marco S: quick design check — I'm iterating on the variant preview micro-interaction in the catalog. when you hover a model row we show a compact preview panel with perf badges + version selector. thinking about keyboard + screen reader signals. screenshot: https://img.redwood/mock/variant-preview.png Katy L: looks good overall. couple of concerns: 1) keyboard focus into the preview isn't obvious, 2) the perf badges feel dense when there are 3-4 of them. can we de-emphasize less-important badges? :thinking_face: Jamal: +1 on badge density. maybe we collapse secondary metrics behind a chevron? primary badge stays visible (latency) and others expand on click/hover. also need to confirm how this behaves in mobile narrow widths. Ava (a11y): a few a11y nits: screen readers shouldn't treat the preview as a separate modal unless we intend to trap focus. if it's transient, use an aria-live region for announcements instead of moving focus. we should also expose an accessible name for the preview panel: `aria-label="Variant preview for "`. :a11y: Marco S: great — I was planning not to trap focus. current prototype moves focus to the version selector on click which felt natural, but I can switch to an aria-live announce for hover-only previews. example:```html Preview opened: resnet-v2-atom1 — latency 84ms, tokens/second 420 ``` Katy L: nice. for keyboard users we still need a visible focus target. suggestion: make the preview reachable via `Tab` from the row and show a subtle focus ring on the panel. that keeps hover/announce behavior for pointer users and explicit focus for keyboard. Jamal: engineering note: if we add a tabbable panel, we should avoid shifting layout on focus (no reflow). maybe overlay the panel with absolute positioning and prefer transform for animation. also let's debounce the aria-live updates (500ms) to avoid announcing flicker when someone mouses across rows. Ava (a11y): debounce is critical. also ensure the perf badges have readable names for screen readers — e.g., `aria-label="latency 84 milliseconds"` not just `latency`. Priya: product context — the main ask from customers is quick compare flows. can the preview include a lightweight "add to compare" affordance? maybe a small checkbox in the panel that maps to the compare table. keeps the row uncluttered. Marco S: yes — plan: compact preview (hover/annouce) + tabbable overlay (enter/tab to open persistent preview) with a small `Add to compare` checkbox, primary badge visible, secondary badges collapsed behind a chevron. accessibility: aria-live announce + aria-label on open + explicit aria-labels for badges + 500ms debounce. Katy L: copy nit: change the badge tooltip copy from `p50 latency` to `Typical latency (p50)` and use sentence case for the preview header. small things but helps consistency. Jamal: implementation checklist from eng side: 1) overlay positioning (transform animations) 2) tabbable panel + focus trap disabled (only trap when user explicitly opens persistent preview) 3) aria-live region + debounce logic 4) expose `data-model-id` for analytics. Ava (a11y): test cases I'll run: NVDA/VoiceOver announce for hover and keyboard open, keyboard-only flow to add to compare, screen reader labelling for each badge, and no double announcements when user tabs quickly. DevBot: deploy-preview created for branch `feat/catalog/preview-a11y` — preview URL: https://staging.redwood/feat-catalog-preview (build #472). :rocket: Priya: decision: prioritize keyboard/a11y fixes for the next patch; badge density changes can follow in the next sprint. please capture PD for release notes and update the catalog docs. Marco S: thanks all — I'll update the figma, push the accessibility changes to the branch, and ping when the deploy is ready for QA. action items: - Marco: update prototype + figma (due EOD) - Jamal: prototype overlay + debounce (PR by Wed) - Ava: test plan & a11y checklist (start after PR) - Katy: microcopy updates & badge priority list Katy L: one last micro-ux ask — when preview is open via keyboard, hitting `Esc` should close and return focus to the row. expected behavior documented. :white_check_mark:
